sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by live-cell imaging with anti-VSV-G/CypHer5 antibody without permeabilization; receptor internalization tracked in real time. Receptor function (signaling) not explicitly reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L2 states the VSV-G tag was introduced 'immediately upstream' of the full-length α1B-AR, meaning it is prepended before residue 1 (M). No signal peptide is present (topology begins O=extracellular at residue 1), so the tag is placed directly on the extracellular N-terminus and is not cleaved. L3 confirms surface display by live-cell imaging without permeabilization. The N-terminal extracellular span (1–44) provides 44 residues of buffer before TM1 at residue 45, making this a sterically unobstructed prepend. Because the paper names no specific residue number but the topology leaves exactly one extracellular terminus, position_evidence is topology_derived. Full-length human α1B-AR with VSV-G epitope tag (YTDIEMNRLGK) inserted immediately upstream (N-terminus) of the receptor, stably and transiently expressed in HEK293 cells for live-cell surface trafficking studies.

literature_notes: Two independent papers (PMC3663791 and PMC9246501) both place tags at the N-terminal extracellular prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) of full-length α1B-AR, using VSV-G and SNAP-tag respectively. No signal peptide is present; the N-terminus (residues 1–44) is directly extracellular. The C-terminal eGFP fusions (L5/L6) are intracellular and recorded in other_positions. No ledger evidence supports any internal extracellular loop (ECL1: 104–119; ECL2: 183–201; ECL3: 317–330) tag insertion for this protein. The two N-terminal sites share the same junction (insert_after_residue = 0) but are grounded in separate papers with different tags; they are reported as two entries per instructions.

literature_other_positions.note: eGFP fused at the C-tail (after residue 520); the C-terminus falls within the intracellular domain (residues 352–520 per topology landmarks), so this is not a surface tag site.
Same C-terminal eGFP construct as L5, described in a second citation from the same paper (PMC10707169); intracellular location confirmed by topology.
